items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: what John Batiste calls his band, Social Music

ctx.x: Is it because now it’s high art?

I think it’s — I don’t know. That’s possible. I think part of it is that, okay getting back to what we talked about quite a while ago, so the overwhelming headline in talking about anything about jazz and all this part of this conversation which we’re having, which is not biographical so much as about the state of jazz, you know there’s this looping headline all the time, which is race, okay? So let’s keep that in mind as it’s floating behind our heads while we’re talking. Okay. So what is it about jazz, how did…

let me back up for a moment. I don’t mean we killed it by putting it in the concert hall, that’s a gloss. What I mean to say is that by taking it away from dancing and by taking it away from good times, what Albert Murray writes about in Stomping the Blues and many, many other places, there was a price to be paid. And the price that was paid that it found its place in the concert hall. Now you might ask yourself the question of why do people, especially in America, but why do we behave the way that we behave in…
